cues.text: The tailor is not always in the shop. That is okay. You can still take care of every tailoring customer the right way.
You can greet the customer and listen to what they want.
You can pin hems, waists, and sleeves, and measure and write it down.
You can take a photo, write the order, give a due date, and quote the price from the POS.
Leave it for the tailor: never promise exactly how it will look.
Wedding and formal gowns, jacket shoulders, and big changes need the tailor.
So do leather, beads, and sequins, making things much bigger, and anything you are not sure about.
Say: our tailor is not in right now, but I can pin it and take your order.
For a hard job, say: our tailor needs to see you for this one. Can we set a time? Then write down their name, phone, and the best time.
